chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whatever increase there is of the humility in the body over what is in the heart, so in our view it is hypocrisy.'

key_terms.الْقَلْبِ: The heart, representing the inner spiritual and cognitive center.
key_terms.خُشُوعُ: Humility, submissiveness, or reverence, particularly in prayer or worship.
key_terms.نِفَاقٌ: Hypocrisy, specifically the state of appearing pious outwardly while lacking that piety inwardly.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of hypocrisy in Shia hadith regarding the relationship between body and heart?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that excessive outward physical humility (khushu') without corresponding inner sincerity is a hallmark of nifaq (hypocrisy), distinguishing it from genuine piety. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the unity of the inner self (batin) and outer action (zahir), where ritual forms must be animated by true spiritual presence. The Prophet’s statement underscores that mere bodily submission without heart-felt devotion is considered insincerity in the sight of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Whatever increase there is of the humility in the body over what is in the ‘Qalb’, so in in ourasws view it is hypocrisy’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd al-Malik from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
If humility expressed physically is more than what is in the heart, in our view it is hypocrisy.’”
